business_summary: Microsoft sells software, cloud computing and devices to businesses, governments and consumers. FY2026 (ended 2026-06-30) revenue was $331.839B, up 18% from $281.724B, across three reported segments: Productivity & Business Processes (Microsoft 365, Teams, LinkedIn, Dynamics) $139.996B; Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products, GitHub) $137.791B; More Personal Computing (Windows, Xbox, Surface, search advertising) $54.052B. Azure passed $100B of annual revenue for the first time in FY2026 and grew 43% in Q4. Most revenue is recurring subscription or consumption-based, and commercial remaining performance obligation (contracted future revenue) reached $678B, up 84%. From FY2027 Microsoft reports in two new segments, 'Agents and Infra' ($268.1B FY2026 revenue recast) and 'Devices and Consumer' ($63.7B). The business should still be winning in 5-10 years because enterprises run their operations on Microsoft software, switching costs are very high, and Microsoft is one of a handful of credible platforms for the AI buildout. The open question this year is not demand but capital intensity: cash capex nearly doubled to $115.948B in FY2026 (plus $24.608B of finance-lease right-of-use assets), so free cash flow FELL to $66.987B from $71.611B even as revenue grew 18%.

moat.type: High switching costs (Microsoft 365, Windows, Azure, Dynamics), network effects (Teams, LinkedIn, GitHub), scale economies in cloud infrastructure, deep enterprise distribution and contracted backlog

quality.roic: ~31% estimated: NOPAT $125.1B (operating income $155.237B x (1 - 19.4% effective tax rate)) on average invested capital ~$405.3B (equity + total debt + finance-lease liabilities - cash and short-term investments, FY2025/FY2026 average). Derived from 10-K figures, not a reported metric.
quality.net_debt_to_ebitda: ~0.15x. Net cash of $36.5B excluding leases ($76.843B cash + short-term investments vs $40.294B total debt); including $66.594B of finance-lease liabilities, net debt is ~$30.0B against EBITDA of ~$199.6B (operating income $155.237B + depreciation $34.3B + intangible amortization $4.7B + finance-lease ROU amortization $5.403B). Finance-lease liabilities have grown from $27.145B (FY2024) to $66.594B (FY2026) and are the fastest-growing obligation on the balance sheet.
quality.fcf_positive: yes, but shrinking: FY2026 FCF $66.987B (operating cash flow $182.935B - capex $115.948B), down from $71.611B in FY2025. Net of $3.101B finance-lease principal payments, $63.886B.

valuation.method: Blend (simple average) of two methods run through code/valuation.py on 2026-10-27. INPUTS UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-17 thesis, deliberately: no new Microsoft financial period has been reported since then (Q1 FY2027 results are due after the close on 2026-10-28), the FY2026 10-K figures were re-verified against SEC XBRL today, and the federal funds range is still 3.75-4.00%. Per the playbook rule, fair value is not moved without a named changed fundamental, and the price rising is not a fundamental. (1) P/E: 26x / 30x / 34x on FY2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS of $17.28 -> $449.28 / $518.40 / $587.52. Base 30x is roughly where a wide-moat ~18% grower with 47% operating margins has historically traded; low = de-rating if AI capex disappoints; high = continued AI-driven acceleration. (2) FCF yield: 3.8% / 3.2% / 2.7% on FY2026 FCF per share of $8.99 ($66.987B / 7,453M diluted shares) -> $236.58 / $280.94 / $332.96; required yields sit roughly in line with a 3.75-4.00% policy rate for a business whose FCF is currently shrinking. Blended band $342.93 / $399.67 / $460.24. Margin of safety at $533.78 = -33.6% (the stock trades 16% ABOVE the high end of our band). For the stock to clear our 12% minimum margin of safety on the base value it would need to trade at or below ~$351.71, about 34% below today. SENSITIVITY, stated honestly: the two methods disagree sharply. On earnings alone MSFT trades at 29.7x trailing GAAP EPS ($17.95) and 30.9x non-GAAP ($17.28); a P/E-only band is $449-$588 with base $518.40, i.e. MSFT is roughly fair (-3.0% margin of safety) on earnings. The blend is pulled down entirely by the FCF method, because cash capex ($115.9B, plus $24.6B of new finance leases) is 3.4x depreciation ($34.3B) and FY2026 FCF fell year over year. Which view is right depends on whether the AI capex earns a return - not yet knowable. We keep the cash-flow method in so the band stays wide and humble.

bull_case: Wide moat intact and arguably widening: commercial remaining performance obligation (contracted future revenue not yet recognised) jumped 84% to $678B in Q4 FY2026, the clearest evidence yet that customers are committing years of spend in advance.
Azure passed $100B of annual revenue in FY2026 and still grew 43% in Q4, with management guiding 44-45% constant-currency growth for Q1 FY2027 - acceleration, not deceleration, at enormous scale.
Exceptional economics: 67.9% gross margin, 46.8% operating margin, ~31% estimated ROIC, and net cash of $36.5B excluding leases. FY2026 net income $133.749B on $331.839B of revenue.
AI is monetising, not just costing: Microsoft 365 Copilot surpassed 30 million paid seats, giving Microsoft a per-seat upsell on an installed base it already owns.
Diversified and durable: Productivity ($140.0B) and Intelligent Cloud ($137.8B) are now similarly sized, so no single product carries the company; FY2026 diluted EPS grew 32% GAAP / 22% non-GAAP.
risks: VALUATION IS THE PRIMARY RISK: at $533.78 MSFT trades ~34% above our base fair value of $399.67 and ~16% above the $460.24 high end of our band. The price has risen ~7% since the 2026-09-17 refresh with no new reported fundamentals, so the gap has widened, not narrowed. The FCF yield at today's price is just 1.68% ($8.99 / $533.78), versus a 3.75-4.00% federal funds rate - less cash yield than cash itself pays.

Event risk in the next 48 hours: Q1 FY2027 results land after the close on 2026-10-28. The stock is near its 250-day high ($543.51) and ~22% above its 200-day average ($437.03), so expectations are high; a miss on Azure growth (guided 44-45% cc) or a capex figure well above $50B could move the price sharply in either direction. Any number in this thesis may be out of date by 2026-10-29.

Free cash flow is going backwards: FY2026 FCF of $66.987B was BELOW FY2025's $71.611B despite 18% revenue growth, because cash capex nearly doubled from $64.551B to $115.948B. Q1 FY2027 capex alone is guided to over $50B. If this continues, FCF could fall again in FY2027.

The AI capex bet is unproven and enormous. Capex ($115.9B) is now 3.4x depreciation ($34.3B), which means today's earnings are flattered relative to the depreciation charge that this asset base will eventually carry. If AI demand disappoints, both margins and returns on capital fall hard.

Off-balance-sheet-ish leverage is building: finance-lease liabilities rose from $27.145B (FY2024) to $46.172B (FY2025) to $66.594B (FY2026). This is real debt-like obligation used to fund datacentres and it does not show up in the headline 'net cash' figure.

Earnings quality: FY2026 GAAP net income ($133.749B) was boosted by discrete items including a $3.2B gain on the Anthropic investment. Non-GAAP net income was $128.786B. Mark-to-market gains on AI-company stakes are not repeatable operating profit.

Macro and rates: the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% with inflation at 3.4%. Higher risk-free rates compress the multiple investors will pay for long-duration growth, and a corporate IT spending slowdown would hit cloud consumption and seat growth.
Regulatory/antitrust scrutiny in the US and EU over cloud bundling, the OpenAI relationship, and AI market power.
Segment reporting changes from FY2027 ('Agents and Infra' / 'Devices and Consumer') reduce comparability and make it harder to track Azure and Windows separately over time.
what_would_break_thesis: Azure constant-currency revenue growth falls below 20% for two consecutive quarters (guidance for Q1 FY2027 is 44-45%; a fall to sub-20% would mean the AI cloud thesis has broken).
Total company revenue declines year over year for two consecutive quarters.
Company-wide gross margin falls below 60% for two consecutive quarters (FY2026: 67.9%).
Operating margin falls below 38% for two consecutive quarters (FY2026: 46.8%) - the signal that AI capex depreciation is overwhelming the P&L.
Free cash flow declines year over year for a third consecutive fiscal year, or turns negative for any full fiscal year (FY2025 $71.6B -> FY2026 $67.0B is already one year of decline).
Net-debt-to-EBITDA including finance-lease liabilities rises above 1.5x (currently ~0.15x), or finance-lease liabilities exceed $150B.
Estimated ROIC falls below 15% on a sustained multi-year basis (currently ~31%).
Commercial remaining performance obligation declines year over year.

A serious accounting restatement, an SEC enforcement action, or a material governance red flag - in particular any restatement of datacentre asset useful lives or of revenue recognised on AI-related related-party transactions.
catalysts: Q1 FY2027 earnings after the close on Wednesday 2026-10-28 (call 2:30 p.m. PT): tests whether Azure hits the guided 44-45% constant-currency growth, whether quarterly capex exceeds $50B, and whether quarterly FCF is still shrinking year over year. This thesis must be refreshed by 2026-10-30 with the 10-Q / 8-K figures.
Evidence of return on AI capex - specifically Intelligent Cloud / 'Agents and Infra' operating margin holding up while the depreciation from the FY2026-27 buildout starts to hit the P&L.

A price pullback toward the $400 base or the $343 low end of our band, which would open a genuine margin of safety. The 250-day closing low from the Alpaca feed is $352.42, so such prices have occurred within the last year - but they are ~34% below today.
Capex growth normalising back toward depreciation, which would cause reported free cash flow to jump sharply and resolve the earnings-versus-cash-flow disagreement in our valuation.
Copilot paid seats compounding well beyond 30 million, proving AI is a revenue line and not just a cost line.
